facts.fact_text: At the material time, the applicant was a member of the "Republic" Party ("Հանրապետություն" կուսակցություն).
On 10 May 2002, the "Republic" Party applied to the Mayor of Yerevan for permission to hold a demonstration on Freedom Square in Yerevan on 14 May 2002.
The demonstration was held as planned on 14 May 2002 at around 15.00 on Freedom Square in Yerevan.
The applicant participated in the demonstration on 14 May 2002 on Freedom Square in Yerevan.
Following the demonstration, at around 16.00 on 14 May 2002, the applicant called on participants to hold a procession through Baghramyan Avenue towards the Parliament building.
A crowd of people followed the applicant in a procession along Baghramyan Avenue towards the Parliament building on 14 May 2002.
On 14 May 2002 at 23.10, the applicant was arrested.

Police officers prepared a record of an administrative offence (վարչական իրավախախտման արձանագրություն) stating that the applicant had "organised an unlawful procession and violated the prescribed rules for holding demonstrations and street processions".

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found that the applicant, in violation of the prescribed rules for holding street processions and demonstrations, on 14 May 2002 at around 16.00, participated with a group of people in an unauthorised procession.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan imposed a fine on the applicant in the amount of 500 Armenian drams (AMD), which was approximately EUR 1 at the material time.

In his appeal to the Civil Court of Appeal, the applicant argued that the interference with his right to freedom of assembly was not prescribed by law, as there did not exist any law which prescribed the rules that the applicant had allegedly violated.
In his appeal to the Civil Court of Appeal, the applicant expressly requested the Civil Court of Appeal to name any law prescribing the rules he had allegedly violated, if such a law existed.

The Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR on "Rules for Organising and Holding of Assemblies, Rallies, Street Processions and Demonstrations in the USSR" of 28 July 1988 defined the requirement of prior authorisation for holding mass events.

Armenia's Declaration of Independence of 23 August 1990 stated that the Supreme Soviet of the Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic, based on the principles enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the general norms of international law, and aiming to achieve the establishment of a democratic society ruled by law, declared that the Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic is renamed as the Republic of Armenia.
Armenia's Declaration of Independence of 23 August 1990 declared that only the Constitution and laws of the Republic of Armenia are valid on the territory of the Republic of Armenia.

Article 11 of the Commonwealth of Independent States Convention of 8 December 1991 provided that from the moment of signing the Convention, norms of third states, including those of the former USSR, shall not be applied on the territories of the signatory states.
Armenia signed the Commonwealth of Independent States Convention on 21 December 1991.
Armenia ratified the Commonwealth of Independent States Convention on 18 February 1992.

Article 116 of the Constitution of the Republic of Armenia of 5 July 1995 provided that from the date of entry into force of the Constitution, the laws and other legal acts of the Republic of Armenia are effective to the extent to which they do not contradict the Constitution.
On 28 April 2004, the Armenian Parliament adopted a law regulating the procedure for holding assemblies, rallies, street processions and demonstrations.

Article 16 of the Law on Holding Assemblies, Rallies, Street Processions and Demonstrations of 28 April 2004 stated that, from the date of its entry into force, the Decree of the Chairmanship of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR on "Rules for Organising and Holding of Assemblies, Rallies, Street Processions and Demonstrations in the USSR" of 28 July 1988 was not to be applied on the territory of the Republic of Armenia.
